findings.claim: The requirement names three unguarded `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites, at reporter lines 735, 1009 and 1101. The diff fixes only two of them: base lines ~985 and ~1077, which match 1009 and 1101 at a constant -24 offset. No hunk touches the site matching reporter line 735 (about base line 711). The new `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` wrapper only filters diagnostics after they are created, and the location is computed before that. So if `[0]` is still indexed there and that path runs for `Item<int>`, the generator and analyzer would still throw `IndexOutOfRangeException`.

findings.claim: `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` drops every diagnostic whose location is not in source, including `Location.None`. That covers source-declared types, not just metadata ones. The new `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` uses `as PropertyDeclarationSyntax`, so for a positional record property (declared by a ParameterSyntax) it returns null. As a result, `BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull` for an in-source positional record property such as `[property: Key((string)null)]` is now silently discarded instead of reported. Before, it threw `InvalidCastException`. The acceptance criteria ask for no crash and for in-assembly types to keep working; they do not ask for errors on source types to disappear.
